description: Get or set the system output volume level (0–100) and mute state of the default output. The get action returns the current level and mute state; on an output with no software volume control, such as many HDMI or DisplayPort displays, both read null and output_device names the device. The set action requires level (0–100), muted (true/false), or both, and fails with volume_unsupported on an output that has no software control for the requested value. Setting level=0 does not mute — use muted=true for explicit muting.

action.description: get returns current state; set applies provided level and/or muted values.

level.description: Output volume level from 0 (silent) to 100 (maximum). Only used with action=set.

muted.description: Mute state. true=mute output, false=unmute. Only used with action=set.

name: macos_control_volume

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `volume_unsupported`: action=set asks for a level or mute state the default output has no software control for. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

level.description: Current output volume level (0–100), or null when the default output has no software volume control.

muted.description: True when the output is muted, or null when the default output has no software mute control.

output_device.description: Name of the default output device. Present only when level or muted is null; null when the device could not be identified.

title: Control macOS Volume
